content.title: When is Earth Day? See 2026 theme, date, events in Florida
content.text: If seeing photos of Earth from the Artemis II mission around the moon gave you a renewed sense of hope, as it did for many, there is a perfect opportunity to celebrate our home planet coming up this month.The 56th annual celebration of Earth Day is less than one week away, with many Earth Day festivals and cleanups planned for around Florida in the next two weekends.Here's what to know about Earth Day 2026, what the theme is this year and a list of Earth Day 2026 events in Florida.Shop sustainable! From Sabai to Zenni, shop top sustainable brands for Earth Month 💚When is Earth Day? Is Earth Day the same day every year?Yes, Earth Day always falls on April 22, no matter the day of the week. This year, Earth Day will fall on Wednesday, April 22, 2026.Striking photo of Earth: Artemis II crew saw a life-changing view. The story of a viral photo.What is the slogan of Earth Day 2026? Why does Earth Day have a theme?The Earth Day 2026 theme is the same as in 2025: “Our power, our planet.""Our Power, Our Planet is Earth Day 2026’s theme, reflecting a fundamental truth: environmental progress doesn’t depend on any single administration or election," the Earth Day website says. "It’s sustained by daily actions of communities, educators, workers, and families protecting where they live and work."According to the website, Earth Day has a theme each year because “introducing a new theme brings attention to the most pressing environmental issues, and themes can bring billions of voices together as one powerful collective pushing for change.”This year's theme being a continuation of the 2025 theme reflects the "limited signs of progress" made in 2025 toward a cleaner environment."2025 was a year marked by extraordinary environmental retrenchment. The current Administration took more than 400 actions ranging from sweeping executive orders to obscure regulatory changes, that are causing irreversible damage to every facet of the global environment," the 2026 theme announcement says."Across the world, environmental safeguards that took generations to defend and create are under relentless attack."How and why did Earth Day start?The first Earth Day was April 22, 1970.The holiday, which isn’t federally observed, was founded by Wisconsin Sen. Gaylord Nelson, who had long been worried about the environment. Nelson wanted to build a movement that combined “the energy of student anti-war protests with an emerging public consciousness about air and water pollution,” according to Earth Day online.With help from a young activist he enlisted to organize college campus teach-ins, Nelson chose April 22 as the day of environmental activism that turned into Earth Day. The movement took flight and gained bipartisan support, even sparking environmentally minded legislation.“Earth Day 1970 achieved a rare political alignment, enlisting support from Republicans and Democrats, rich and poor, urban dwellers and farmers, business and labor leaders,” the Earth Day website’s history of the holiday says.“By the end of 1970, the first Earth Day led to the creation of the United States Environmental Protection Agency and the passage of other first-of-their-kind environmental laws, including the National Environmental Education Act, the Occupational Safety and Health Act, and the Clean Air Act. Two years later, Congress passed the Clean Water Act.”Celebrate Earth Day in Florida: How to find an Earth Day event near youEarth Day’s Great Global Cleanup, which is an ongoing campaign outside of just one day a year, “aims to rid the world of waste and plastic pollution for good.”To find an Earth Day-organized cleanup or event near you this April, you can use the interactive map on the Earth Day site.Here are just a few of the Earth Day 2026 events in Florida, according to the Earth Day map:Note that many of these are events that require registration before attending.Earth Day 2026 Community Clean-Up, Jacksonville Beach and St. Augustine: "Join our 2-location cleanup — we’ll bring the supplies, you bring the energy! Let’s make a difference together. You can find us at Seawalk Pavilion in Jacksonville Beach & in St. Augustine Beach in front of the Dance Company!" Starts at 9 a.m. on Saturday, April 18.Beach Squad Beach Cleanup, Daytona Beach: "Join Beach Squad for our public beach cleanup. These cleanups are open to individuals, families, and small groups of 4 or fewer." Starts at 8:30 a.m. at Sun Splash Park on Sunday, April 26.3rd Annual Earth Day Community Clean-Up, Orlando: "Get your hands dirty & your heart full at our Earth Day Clean-Up event! Let's make a splash for a cleaner, greener downtown community!" Starts at 9 a.m. at the tailgate lot at Inter&Co Stadium on Sunday, April 19.4th Annual Lake Wilson Clean Up Bash 2026, Lake Wilson (Osceola County): "Come help us clean up the best place on earth! Please RSVP by April 18th to paige.m.kraus@gmail.com so we can make sure we have enough pizza!" Starts at 10 a.m. on Saturday, April 25.St. Lucie Earth Day Festival, Port St. Lucie: "The festival showcases unique eco-art, sustainable living ideas, outdoor recreation opportunities and community resources. Local organizations and businesses will share hands-on activities in six unique “neighborhoods” throughout the gardens and trails of the preserve. Meet local environmental groups, civic groups, education professionals, foresters, gardeners, beekeepers and more." Starts at 10 a.m. on Saturday, April 18.Young Friends April Beach Cleanup 2026 - Friends of Jupiter Beach, Jupiter: "This is a fantastic opportunity to make a positive impact on our beautiful coastline, meet new friends, and enjoy a fun and fulfilling afternoon." Starts at 3 p.m. on Sunday, April 19.City of Boynton Beach Earth Month Event 2026, Boynton Beach: "The event will feature local, eco-friendly vendors, food trucks, live music, family-friendly activities, and a tree and rain barrel giveaway for Boynton Beach residents." Beach cleanup starts at 9 a.m. on Saturday, April 25.Parrot Beach Cleanup, Fort Lauderdale: "Join us for our monthly Beach Clean Up. We provide all garbage grabbers, buckets & water. We also sign off on any community service hours you may need!" Starts at 11 a.m. on Saturday, April 18.Miami Earth Day Bash 2026, Miami Beach: "This free, family-friendly event invites the community to take part in a marine debris clean-up, habitat restoration with Frost Science’s MUVE program (separate RSVP required), environmental education, and hands-on community-based activities that support the health of Biscayne Bay." Starts at 9 a.m. on Saturday, April 18.Naples Pier Beach Cleanup, Naples: "Please join us at our beach cleanup where we provide everything, including tools, water, and snacks. All we need is you!" Starts at 9:30 a.m. on Saturday, April 25.Earth Day Riverwalk Clean Up, Tampa: "Join us for our next Riverwalk Clean-Up on Earth Day with Keep Tampa Bay Beautiful!" Starts at 8 a.m. on Wednesday, April 22.Earth Day Cleanup: 4th Street North Mangroves, St. Pete: "Join Keep Pinellas Beautiful for a cleanup at the 4th Street North Mangroves in honor of Earth Day! This Keep America Beautiful signature event engages thousands of volunteers, removing litter and beautifying locations throughout Pinellas County." Starts at 9 a.m. on Wednesday, April 22.2026 Great American Cleanup & Tire Roundup, Gainesville: "Join Keep Alachua County Beautiful for our annual Great American Cleanup alongside a community Tire Roundup event as residents and volunteers come together to remove litter and beautify areas throughout Gainesville." Starts at 8 a.m. on Saturday, April 25.Tallahassee Earth Day Festival, Tallahassee: "A festival with educational activities, workshops, and eco-friendly vendors." Starts at 11:30 a.m. on Saturday, April 25.Lianna Norman is a trending reporter for the USA TODAY NETWORK-Florida, covering pop culture, lotteries, rocket launches, Florida wildlife, breaking news and more.
